About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Why we're looking for you

 

We’re building a highly impactful, data & AI-first Product Analytics function at Owner.com http://Owner.com. As a Senior Associate, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the product roadmap through close collaboration with Product Managers to establish opportunity impact sizing, product effectiveness tracking, and direct product strategy & tactical contributions. 

Your work will shift to wherever the highest impact lies - whether that's deep root-cause analysis on product opportunity areas, sizing the expected impact of new features to shape engineering priorities, designing & providing visibility to product health metrics, or directly contributing to the development of analytics and AI-powered product features. The best candidates will not simply provide insights to the EPD (Engineering & Product) org, but be a strategic and operational driver, identifying gaps/opportunities, recommending product roadmap improvements, and creating overall meaningful business impact through direct influence on the product.

 

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada.

 

You should apply if you ...

 

 - Have felt torn about whether to pursue a business vs pure technical/analytical career path (at Owner, we believe these must merge)

 - Identify inefficiencies in everyday life - and see them as exciting opportunities.

 - Aren't satisfied with understanding things at a surface level, and get satisfaction from understanding the root cause (the WHY)

 - When solving problems, you enjoy diving deeply in them to understand root causes and become a "subject matter expert”, but know when to stop “overbuilding”

 - Aren't afraid of and enjoy picking up new skills and tools to problem-solve

 - Enjoy tinkering and testing (or building) applications for AI tools like Claude Code, Codex

 - Want to build solutions for lasting processes and systems. Love a good data-driven decision-making process (but also understand when this is possible and when it isn't)

 - Have a proven track record of collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.
   
   

The impact you'll have



 - Influence Product Planning Roadmap: Influence product planning through informative impact sizing, enabling more strategic decision-making for Owner.

 - Uncover Product Gaps, and Recommend/Action Resolutions: Analyze the root cause for product success metric gaps and issues, and recommend immediate resolution pathways, or action them yourself.

 - Own Your Product Pod’s Analytics: Improve the analytics and engagement strategy for your product pod(s). This isn't just an insights role - you'll design and ship data products and automated AI workflows that enable teams to act on data without waiting for analysis.

 - Tackle emerging priorities: Lead or contribute to ad hoc projects as business needs arise; this role flexes with what matters most.

 - Ultimately, help grow our customers’ sales and improve their experience: Across all product pods, the mission is uniform: improve our customer’s experience and help customers grow their sales with Owner.com http://Owner.com.



Who you’ll work with



 - Reporting Structure: This role reports directly to Mark Rogal, Manager, Product Analytics & Applied AI

 - Team Collaboration: You will be embedded within up to two product squads (preferably one), working closely with Product Managers, designers, and developers within their regular sprint cadence.

 - Technical Collaboration: You will collaborate with Analytics Engineers on all technical aspects, including data modeling, data quality, and the use of tools like DBT and Snowflake.

 - Executive Visibility: The work in this role directly drives product strategy, which means regular exposure to senior and executive leadership.



What we're looking for



 - 4+ years in analytics, strategy, or ops - whether that's management consulting, startup analytics, or a hybrid path that's hard to label

 - Extremely strong quantitative skills, with additional technical background or education strongly preferred. SQL/Python/Claude Code/Codex and product analytics experience is a strong plus

 - You've built things - dashboards, tools, processes - not just delivered decks

 - You dig into root causes until you actually understand the problem, not just the symptoms

 - Comfortable with ambiguity; you don't need a playbook to figure out what to work on next

 - Experience with SaaS, marketplaces, or high-growth startups preferred

 - Restaurant industry experience is a plus
   
   
   

Compensation and benefits

 - The estimated base salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000 USD depending on such factors such as level, experience and location. The offer will also include a generous pre-IPO equity package

 - Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, remote first, unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!



What our interview process looks like



Step 1: Recruiter Phone Screen

Begin with a conversation with a recruiter to evaluate your background, better understand what you’re looking for in your next opportunity, and answer any early questions you may have about the role or company.

 

Step 2: Hiring Manager Interview

Participate in a 45-minute video interview with the hiring manager. This conversation will go deeper into your experience, approach to work, and views on problem-solving and collaboration.

 

Step 3: Technical Case Study (Pass/Fail)

Receive a technical case study to complete independently. You will have seven days to submit your assignment. The team will review your submission and provide detailed feedback on whether you have passed or not passed this stage.

 

Step 4: Full Round / Case Study Presentation

If you pass the technical case study, you'll move forward to a 60-minute presentation round with several members of the Business Operations team. You'll walk the team through your approach, thought process, and recommendations, and answer live follow-up questions.

 

Step 5: Final / Executive Interviews

The final stage consists of one to two executive interviews with C-suite leadership team members. These 30-minute conversations focus on overall alignment, communication, strategic thinking, and long-term fit with the business.





Notice - Employment Scams

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.



We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

Hi, I’m Geo, Ashby’s VP of Product. I joined Ashby August ‘26; read more about why I joined here. https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/all/a-letter-from-chris-geoghegan-on-joining-ashby I’m hiring for multiple Product Managers who will report directly to me. More on the specific product areas below.

At Ashby, we have a unique approach to building products https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles. As a PM, your primary goal is to eliminate frustration and bring delight to our customers. You’ll work with engineers who deeply understand the customer and business problem and own the solution end-to-end. This means that you spend less time writing detailed specs and more time with customers and doing deep product thinking.

Our unique approach is working. We’re growing >100% year over year and have notable customers such as Notion, Linear, OpenAI, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best in class among our peers. We’re backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more!



PRODUCT AREAS

From day one, we have aimed to build "all-in-one and best-in-class" software for Talent teams. In addition to building a multi-product foundation from day one, we have also focused on enabling customizability and power-user features while keeping Ashby easy to get started with. Doing both is an ambitious undertaking!

We want to continue down this ambitious path in future and add multiple new products, which means we:

 - Are not just building a product, we’re building a platform

 - Need to find a balance between re-usable building blocks and feature-specific behaviour

 - Blend enterprise customizability and ease of use

We also want to continuously delight users. We hear "I never thought one could fall in love with an ATS" quite often, and we want to keep that true for all future products we build.

We are looking for Product Managers who can own the roadmap and strategy for the following areas:

 1. Outbound Sourcing: You’ll build a platform that enables teams to hire sourcing agents directly from Ashby. Customers simply write the job description, and agents start booking calls with highly qualified candidates.

 2. Product Platform: Ashby was designed from the beginning as a multi-product platform. We’re looking for a PM to establish this team and own the shared building blocks, foundational capabilities, and APIs that let product teams move quickly.

 3. AI Platform: You’ll own the Ashby Assistant, Ashby MCP, and the AI platform used across many product surfaces. You’ll help drive shared primitives, such as AI memory and context.

During the interview process, we’ll determine which role you're best suited for. We’re also advertising this opening as Staff Product Manager. Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience.




YOUR ROLE

 - Drive Impact: Deeply understand our customers and ship impactful product improvements and investments to maintain our strong velocity.

 - Quality: Apply your strong product taste and sound judgement to deliver solutions that are both powerful and a joy to use. Use your judgment to identify areas where we need to improve quality before shipping.

 - Prioritization and Strategy: Maintain a roadmap to ensure engineering is never blocked, and set a compelling strategy and vision for the next 6-18 months.

 - Customer Research: Spend time with customers and customer-facing teams. Synthesize customer feedback, research, and competitive intel to drive smart prioritization choices.

 - Execution Excellence: Set the pace for your product area by identifying bottlenecks, scoping effectively, and driving projects toward high-impact releases. Stay close to engineering work to navigate tradeoffs, manage technical risks, and resolve execution challenges.

 - Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner across go-to-market teams to bring the features and products your team builds to the market. Anticipate and plan for the needs to help inform pricing, marketing, and customer support.

 - Ownership and reliability: follow through on commitments, manage time ruthlessly, respond promptly to stakeholders, and communicate proactively when priorities or timelines change.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You have an unnatural curiosity and excitement about the end-user and the jobs they do

 - You bring an Engineering mindset to product problems and can think through edge cases and understand how to extend our underlying platform to create leverage

 - You can demonstrate taste - you care about the quality of the products you build and use

 - You're an excellent writer and synthesizer; you bring product knowledge and clarity to the entire organization and enable Engineers with product insights

 - You can build a thesis for prioritization and communicate priorities using a sound strategy that combines principled thinking, research, and data

 - You leverage tools and processes to build operational excellence into your product process

 - You have a strong business sense and understand how product and GTM should collaborate, how your features may be monetized, and how product priorities fit into larger business priorities




YOU MAY NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You prefer to specify exactly what Engineering should build rather than give engineers room to own the solution.

 - You dislike written documentation and prefer to manage the team via meetings and quick Slack messages.

 - You’re primarily interested in shipping features and not thinking through how to make them reusable platform capabilities.

 - You don’t enjoy doing deep research yourself and prefer to outsource that UX research, market research, and data teams.

 - You’re uncomfortable moving with urgency, making tradeoffs, and reprioritizing when new information emerges.

 - You’re primarily motivated by achieving a metric more than delivering a great product experience for customers.




WE WORK DIFFERENTLY

At Ashby, the role of Product Managers is different from what I’ve seen in most product orgs. At a high level, PMs are responsible for shipping impactful product changes at high velocity, consistently and over an extended period. When we think about impactful product changes, our primary goal is to remove frustration and add delight.

At many organizations, PMs are required to write detailed specs that handle every edge case. Designers are required to mock up every pixel. At Ashby, it’s different. We believe individual contributors do their best work when they have a deep understanding of the end user and the business, and ownership of the solution. This is reflected in the engineers Ashby hires: they own projects end-to-end and deeply understand the problems they are solving. PMs are expected to give significant white space in their specs. As a result, PMs can spend less time managing tickets and more time with customers and thinking deeply about the product strategy.

At Ashby, PMs need to be the pace-setters for their product areas. This means they bring a healthy level of impatience and time-paranoia to the table. This does not mean cutting corners or demanding that engineers work unreasonable hours. As a PM, you can help engineers by managing the project scope well, identifying when it’s appropriate to bring in help, or being ruthless about prioritization.

For PM roles at Ashby, we believe great products are built through deep thinking and a clear understanding of user needs. A major part of your role involves conducting thorough user research to uncover underlying customer problems and translating those insights into well-reasoned product strategies.

Finally, Ashby isn’t simply an ATS. Right from the foundations, it was designed to be much more than that. It’s a platform modelled around how organizations (from early-stage startups to massive enterprises) think about recruiting, managing, and retaining top talent. As a PM at Ashby, you should, over time, get familiar with our most common building blocks. You’ll invest not only in product improvements but in platform thinking.





INTERVIEW PROCESS

If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates that advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect:

 1. Intro Call - 30 mins

 2. Product Experience Deep Dive - 45 mins

 3. Product Exercise - 1 hour

 4. Final Round Interview - 2 hours
    Mostly focused on cross-functional Interviews to meet more of the team. This is a critical hire for us and a role that will touch a lot of functions - we want to make sure you'll meet folks you'll be working closely with




BENEFITS

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year.

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, which is also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

To request reasonable accommodations, please contact hiring@ashbyhq.com.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

Hi! 👋 I'm Chris https://www.linkedin.com/in/chkrlee/, head of Product Design at Ashby.

We're looking for a versatile, intrinsically motivated designer who is excited to contribute to rethinking how modern software is designed. At Ashby, you'll be part designer, part product manager, part consultant, and part design system manager (or some combination of the 4!). We do design differently here, and if that excites you, read on.

Our unique approach is working - we're growing >100% year-over-year and have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, very low churn, and many years of runway. We're backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more! We’ll share more details once we meet.




HOW WE WORK

In my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. This may sound familiar to you! The product manager briefs the designer who then designs. After designing, mocks are handed to the engineers. 

We take a more principled approach here at Ashby. If you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project. Sometimes in the past, I'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation I had written. Other times, I felt I should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end. In these latter cases, it made sense that I was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.

This principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed Ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. We don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.

Currently, I report to Benji, the co-founder & CEO. Both Abhik and Benji (our founders) care deeply about design, which at first glance may seem counterintuitive given the number of full-time designers that we employ. The belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title. 

The design department’s job at Ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that PMs/Engineers choose to make. That, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves. 



Separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on IC-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. While you get the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup, you also get the agency and no-nonsense, no-red-tape culture of a seed-stage startup.




WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

Talent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. To accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. Teams struggle to keep up!



Scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges. A recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes. They must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 



Ashby provides talent teams with intelligent and powerful software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We put a lot of effort into designing products that are approachable to beginners but mastered and extended by power users. In many ways, spreadsheets set the bar here (and are what we often replace!).




WHY YOU SHOULD OR SHOULDN’T APPLY




YOUR QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 10+ years of product design experience, with the majority being in desktop SaaS

 - Able to take huge, ambiguous projects and break them down into actionable parts 

 - Able to speak to patterns of the highest functioning design teams and how to create an environment of high performance

 - Able to leverage designers' superpowers to influence engineering, product, and the rest of the company

 - Able to create standards and principles that will help improve the quality of design across the product org

 - Able to think from first principles instead of simply applying the “standard” UX processes.

 - Enough experience that your intuition can solve most usability problems without having to rely solely on data & metrics or conducting user research.

 - Curious & resourceful enough to come up with creative solutions and de-risk them appropriately.

 - Best-in-class skills in layout, navigation, IA, UI, and interaction design.

 - Obsession with craft & details.

 - You have experience at an early-stage startup or have spent time as a solo designer on a team.




YOU MAY WANT TO APPLY IF YOU’RE EXCITED ABOUT:

 - Creating leverage and impact far and above what you'd see in a typical EPD product team structure. You won’t be a cog in the wheel, the wheel is not very big!

 - Getting to work on all parts of a massive product surface area - spanning many user types, JTBDs, usability challenges, etc. Unlike in other organizations, you won’t be stuck working on one problem for many years.

 - Helping reinvent the design model for modern enterprise software—you don’t have to build wireframes, user journeys, personas, etc. What matters is solving a customer’s problem; what tools you use are up to you.

 - Covering all parts of the design process with a focus on design craft. You'll still be doing the occasional user research interview but will be focused on using heuristics & experience to improve our IA, navigation, interactions, UI patterns, and more.

 - Helping build our design system from (almost) the ground up.


CONVERSELY, YOU MAY NOT WANT TO APPLY IF:

 - You feel uncomfortable designing independently without much guidance from a PM or design management.

 - You’re uncomfortable having your decisions and process being challenged constantly by engineering & product.

 - You prefer an in-person role over remote (Ashby operates remotely).

 - You dislike written documentation.

 - You want a set structure and rhythm to your projects.
   
   - PM gives you a brief, you do wireframes, then mocks, then pass off work to engineers. Rinse and repeat.

 - You prefer a narrow job scope - interaction design only, design system only, etc.


ON A WEEKLY BASIS YOU WILL FIND YOURSELF:

 - Consulting for engineers who need help structuring layout, typography, flows, etc.

 - Digging into problems by consulting GTM, talking to customers, asking for data requests, and more in order to present confident assumptions about your proposals.

 - Using Figma to draw out your ideas and create visual artifacts for stakeholder alignment.

 - Writing specification docs (we call them specs!) that detail your design proposals. These documents are meant to get stakeholder alignment on the biggest decisions you want to make and are a core part of how we work at Ashby.

 - Taking ownership of larger product features and thinking through Jobs-To-Be-Done, navigation, information architecture, layout, interaction, etc.

 - Taking in customer feedback and using heuristics to build your own usability backlog and propose projects for engineers to take on.

 - Consolidating and refining our design system to be functional, aesthetic, and best-in-class.


INTERVIEW PROCESS

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together and talking through decisions. Our interview process is four rounds with some casual Zoom coffee in between to get to know each other: 

 1. 30m introduction call to discuss Ashby and your experience

 2. 45m portfolio review

 3. 75m design exercise and app teardown. The exercise will be a live whiteboarding exercise where we provide a prompt and you show us how you'd break down problems and come up with solutions. 

 4. 2.5hr final round - meet the team + portfolio repeat with a founder

I'll be your main point of contact and prepare you for interviews. You’ll meet other engineers and product managers as well (with lots of time to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer by the last round, I'll provide feedback as to why if you'd like it (I'm serious!).




BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. This is one of the reasons I joined personally - not a lot of startups do this.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it.

 - Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

 New markets. Fintech is one of the fastest-growing parts of Jobber, and a core strategic priority for us as a company. We're investing in this area because we believe embedding financial tools within our product deepens our ability to help small businesses be successful—whether that's helping them get paid through Jobber Payments, or, in the near future, offering them access to capital through a growing lending business.

Our Risk team is a critical part of the broader Fintech team, and core to Jobber's success. Credit Risk is responsible for the frameworks, models, and operational discipline that let us extend payments and lending products responsibly, protecting both our customers and Jobber from undue credit exposure.



The Role:

The Manager, Credit Risk will lead and grow a team of Credit Risk Analysts, owning the day-to-day operations of the credit risk function while helping build it into something more ambitious: an AI-native credit risk practice, built for Jobber Payments today and ready to scale into a growing lending business. This is a role for a builder, not a doer—someone who looks at a manual process or an ad hoc decision and asks how it should be automated, modeled, or systematized, rather than simply executed by hand.

You'll work closely with Data Science and Risk Analytics to design and strengthen credit risk models, policies, and monitoring, and you'll partner cross-functionally across Fintech, Product, and Customer Support to make sure credit risk decisions are embedded seamlessly into the products our customers use every day.



The Manager, Credit Risk will:

 - Lead, coach, and grow a team of Credit Risk Analysts, setting the standard for how the team investigates, decisions, and communicates credit risk.

 - Own credit risk operations end-to-end: underwriting and exposure decisions, portfolio monitoring, loss forecasting, and reporting on credit risk performance and trends.

 - Partner closely with Data Science and Risk Analytics to build, validate, and improve credit risk models and decisioning logic, including scorecards, statistical models, and machine learning approaches where they add value.

 - Champion an AI-native approach to credit risk management—using AI and automation to build novel solutions to novel problems, not just to speed up existing workflows.

 - Build and strengthen the credit risk function for Jobber's payments business today, and lay the groundwork for credit risk management of a growing lending business.

 - Work cross-functionally with Fintech, Product, and Customer Support teams to embed credit risk policy and controls into product and operational workflows.

 - Develop a credit risk provisioning process and reserving practices building from IFRS9 or equivalent GAAP standards, partnering with Finance and Accounting as needed.

 - Identify opportunities to automate manual credit risk processes and drive them from idea through to implementation.

 - Report on credit risk exposure, portfolio health, and emerging trends to Fintech and Risk leadership.

 - Support broader Fintech and Risk initiatives on credit-risk-relevant topics, including vendor evaluations and new product launches.



To be successful, you should have:

 - Demonstrated experience in credit risk, in financial services, fintech, payments, or lending, including people leadership or mentorship of an analyst team.

 - A builder's mindset: a track record of solving problems through automation and tooling, not just process, and genuine enthusiasm for using AI to build new approaches to credit risk rather than only applying existing ones.

 - A deeply data-centric approach to decision-making, with comfort working directly in the data rather than relying solely on others to produce it for you.

 - Proficiency in SQL and Python (or a similar language), enough to independently pull, analyze, and interrogate data and to collaborate credibly with Data Science and Analytics.

 - Familiarity with IFRS9 or equivalent GAAP standards (e.g., CECL) for credit loss provisioning, or a strong ability to learn and apply this quickly.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical or quantitative findings into decisions that product, operations, and leadership stakeholders can act on.

 - The ability to embrace ambiguity and change—we don't know what we don't know, so you should be comfortable coming in and improving the process rather than waiting for one to be handed to you.

About the Role 
 Nelson Education is seeking a Corporate Accountant to join the Accounting team, reporting to the Manager, Accounting. The Corporate Accountant plays a key role in the monthly financial close, with responsibility for preparing and maintaining account reconciliations, journal entries, supporting schedules and analysis across the balance sheet.
 The role is accountable for the accuracy and completeness of the accounts it owns and is expected to understand and explain the activity behind those balances. The Corporate Accountant also supports the external audit, contributes to process documentation and improvement, and works closely with colleagues across Finance and the business to ensure accounting information is complete and reliable.
 This is an opportunity for an accountant with hands-on month-end experience to take ownership of increasingly complex areas, build deeper IFRS and systems expertise, and grow toward broader financial reporting responsibility with direct coaching from the Manager, Accounting.
 Key Accountabilities 
 Month-End Close & Account Reconciliations 
 Own assigned areas of the monthly close, including account reconciliations, journal entries, supporting schedules and balance sheet roll forwards, ensuring balances are accurate, supported and fully explained.
 Prepare and maintain accounting schedules and entries for areas such as accruals, fixed assets, intangible assets, royalties and other assigned accounts.
 Prepare royalty calculations, author and licensor statements, accruals and payment schedules in accordance with contract terms, and prepare the annual tax reporting for royalty recipients, including T4A and related slips.
 Prepare or support GST/HST and other indirect tax filings and reconciliations for assigned accounts.
 Investigate and resolve reconciling items, unusual movements and accounting issues, partnering with the Manager, Accounting on matters requiring judgment or review before entries are posted.
 Manage assigned close activities in accordance with the close calendar, proactively identifying and escalating issues that could affect deadlines or financial reporting.
 Prepare analysis and variance explanations for accounts owned and contribute to the monthly financial reporting process.
 Analysis & Reporting Support 
 Prepare supporting schedules and respond to audit requests for assigned accounts, ensuring information is complete, accurate and provided on a timely basis.
 Support the preparation of annual financial statement disclosures and other financial reporting requirements.
 Support financial analysis and reporting activities, including gross margin and SG&A analysis, through data extraction, reconciliation and analysis.
 Process Ownership & Improvement 
 Own and maintain documented procedures for assigned accounting areas, ensuring processes are current, well controlled and can be consistently performed by others.
 Identify and implement improvements to the efficiency, accuracy and consistency of reconciliation and close processes through better documentation, templates, system capabilities and automation.
 Build strong working knowledge of NetSuite, including reporting, saved searches, journal posting and period-close activities, and use system capabilities to improve the processes owned.
 Develop broader knowledge of the Accounting function and progressively take ownership of more complex accounting areas.
 Teamwork & Collaboration 
 Partner with the Manager, Accounting on the close calendar and review findings, and proactively communicate issues and recommendations.
 Partner with the Manager, Reporting on NetSuite reporting, data extracts and automation of recurring entries, and with AR & AP Operations, Supply Chain and other functions to ensure the completeness and accuracy of information supporting assigned accounts.
 Provide backup and support for other areas of the close and share knowledge as responsibilities expand.
 Contribute to a collaborative Finance team and take on additional projects and responsibilities as business needs evolve.
 Post-secondary degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline; CPA designation or active enrolment in the CPA program strongly preferred.
 3+ years of progressive accounting experience, including hands-on month-end close and account reconciliation responsibilities.
 Solid understanding of accounting principles, with working knowledge of IFRS; familiarity with GST/HST is an asset.
 Experience with balance sheet accounting, including areas such as accruals, fixed assets and other reconciliations; exposure to royalty or other contract-based calculations is an asset.
 Experience supporting an external audit.
 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience with NetSuite or another ERP system.
 Strong analytical, organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple deliverables and deadlines independently.
 Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a collaborative, curious and continuous-improvement mindset.
 Who You Are

Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans - by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting text output, you will improve Large Language Model’s performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere’s tech.


Cohere seeks dynamic and dedicated Data Annotators with exceptional Modern Standard German Writing, Translation, and Data Manipulation skill.

 - Label and Rank: Accurately label and rank machine learning data with advanced proficiency in German, ensuring data integrity and quality.

 - Audit and Correct: Scrutinize and rectify any inaccuracies in language data (may include text, image, JSON, TSV/CSV, Markdown), maintaining the highest standard of data accuracy.

 - Reading and Text-Based Tasks: Efficiently complete reading and text-based assignments, with high attention to detail.

 - Preference-Based Tasks: Evaluate and complete tasks, assessing which responses in German best conform to project guidelines.

 - Recommend Optimizations: Identify and suggest opportunities for improving data quality and model performance in German language tasks.

 - Provide Feedback: Collaborate and communicate effectively, providing feedback to cross-functional team members, particularly on German language-related matters.

 - Detail-Oriented Execution: Maintain meticulous attention to detail while performing repetitive and precise tasks, particularly when working with language data.

 - Language Proficiency: Native or near-native proficiency in German; excellent command over English.

 - Expert reading and writing skills - which you are ready to prove on our written test.

 - Basic familiarity with JSON/TSV/CSV/Markdown data manipulation.

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy - you’re the type to proofread all of your emails!

 - Ability to follow complex instructions, navigate ambiguity and work independently.

 - Superb sense of urgency and time management.

WANTED: One Hungry Closer Who's Sick Of Selling Other People's Dreams. 
 (Read this whole thing. If you quit halfway, we already have your answer.) 
 Most job ads read like they were written by HR. 
Bullet points. Buzzwords. 
A "competitive compensation package" that translates to "we'll pay you just enough to keep you from leaving, but never enough to actually win." 
 This isn't that.
 This is a letter. From us to you. About one of the most lopsided opportunities we've ever put in front of a salesperson and the rare, specific human being we're trying to find to fill it.
 If that human is you, you're going to feel it in your chest somewhere around paragraph nine.
 First — Who We Are. And Why It Matters. 
 We're Wealth Without Wall Street. 
 Russ Morgan and Joey Muré built this from scratch, not in a Manhattan glass tower, not with a hedge-fund pedigree, but by getting fed up watching hardworking business owners hand their financial futures to suit-wearing strangers who couldn't pick them out of a lineup.
 Together we've helped thousands of business owners, real estate investors, doctors, and high-earning professionals do what 99% of America has been brainwashed into believing is impossible:
 Generate passive income that exceeds their monthly expenses. 
 That's the whole game. That's what freedom actually looks like — not a 401(k) you can't touch until you're 65 and your knees are gone, but real cash flowing in every single month whether you work or not.
 We do it using the Infinite Banking Concept — the same wealth strategy quietly used by the richest families in America for over a century. We teach people to become their own bank. To recycle their capital. To stop renting money from institutions that profit off their ignorance.
 Russ and Joey have done it themselves. Over $50,000 per month in passive income. Co-authors of an Amazon bestseller. Hosts of one of the most respected podcasts in personal finance.
 This isn't theory. This is the real thing.
 Right now, we have more qualified people waving their hands than we can possibly talk to.
 That's where you come in.
 The Role: Business Developer. (Translation: The Person Who Decides Who Gets Free.) 
 Let us describe a typical day so you know exactly what you're signing up for.
 You wake up. You check your calendar. There are real, pre-qualified humans on it, people who registered for our workshops, devoured Russ and Joey's content, raised their hand, and said "I want a Passive Income Game Plan Session." 
 These aren't cold strangers. 
These aren't leads scraped off a list. 
These are people who already trust the brand, already believe the philosophy, and already know they're tired of the rat race.
 Your job is to pickup the phone, set appointments by making outbound calls and take inbound appointments.
Ask the kind of questions most salespeople are too soft to ask. 
Find out where they really are financially, emotionally, mentally. Diagnose whether IBC and our path is actually right for them.
 And if it is? You hand them the keys.
 You're not pitching. You're not pressuring. You're not chasing.
 You're the bridge between someone's current life — exhausted, overworked, financially fragile — and the version of their life where they sleep through the night because money is finally working for them instead of against them.
 That's the job.
 If that sounds like too much responsibility, the back button is right there.
 Who We Are NOT Looking For. 
 Let's save us both some time.
 We are not looking for the guy who calls himself a "closer" because he sold timeshares in Cabo for six months.
 We are not looking for the person who needs a six-week ramp, a personal coach, three resource Slack channels, and a "psychologically safe" environment to dial a phone.
 We are not looking for someone who's going to ghost on Friday afternoons because the surf is up.
 We are not looking for a salary chaser. If a guaranteed paycheck is what you're after, McDonald's is hiring. Go thrive.
 And we are definitely not looking for someone who can't speak from the heart about money, freedom, and the very real fear most Americans carry around about both. If you can't connect at the soul level, you can't sell this. Period.
 Who We ARE Looking For. 
 A killer. But a killer with a conscience.
 Someone who can sit across a Zoom screen from a stranger and — within ten minutes — have them admitting things they haven't told their spouse.
 Someone who's already a top performer somewhere else and is bored to tears selling SaaS, solar, or something else they couldn't care less about.
 Someone who reads Rich Dad Poor Dad , listens to BiggerPockets, follows Dave Ramsey just to argue with him, and already has an opinion about whole life insurance — even if that opinion needs updating.
 Someone with the spine to say "I don't think you're a fit. Here's why," and walk away from money on principle.
 Someone who treats every conversation like it's their last shot — because that's how the great ones do it.
 If you read those five paragraphs and felt seen, keep going.
 The Non-Negotiables.
 Proven sales background. Minimum 2+ years closing in a high-ticket, phone/Zoom-based environment. We don't care about your resume — we care about your numbers.
 25%+ close rate after probation. Below that, you're not the right fit and we'll part as friends.
 Full ownership of your pipeline. Nobody is going to chase you to follow up. The leads are there. The CRM is built. The systems work. You just have to work them. 
 Show up sharp every single day. This is a high-tempo environment. We move. We measure. We adjust.
 Live the message. If you don't believe building wealth outside the traditional system is possible, you cannot sell it. Period. Bonus points if you already own a whole life policy, have read Becoming Your Own Banker by Nelson Nash, or have personal experience with real estate investing or passive income.
 Stable, professional remote setup. High-speed internet, quiet environment, quality camera and mic. We're representing a premium brand on every single call.
 CRM discipline. You log notes the same day. You update statuses in real time. If "I forgot to update the CRM" is a phrase that comes out of your mouth more than twice, this won't work.
 Emotional intelligence over scripts. We'll give you frameworks. We will not give you a robot script to memorize. If you can't read a human, you can't sell here.
 Coachable ego. Strong opinions, loosely held. We promote killers who listen. We fire prima donnas who don't.
 A worldview that aligns. You believe people are responsible for their own freedom. You believe Wall Street is not the answer for most families. You believe in earning the right to be paid well — not waiting to be handed it.
 The Catch: 
 We get a lot of applications. 
Most won't make it past the first filter. 
We're not looking for a resume, we're looking for evidence. 
 A sales background that proves you can sit in the fire without flinching, a track record that doesn't need to be inflated, and a worldview that aligns with what we actually believe about money, freedom, and the responsibility of helping someone change their life.
 If that's you, apply. Right now. While you're feeling it.
 The Compensation. (Read This Slowly.) 
 We're going to lay this out plainly because we want you to do the math before you apply, not after.
 100% commission. Uncapped. No ceiling. No politics. 
 10% of cash collected on all Passive Income Lab Sales ($7,500 Price Point)
 20% of cash collected on all PIOS Sales ($1,000 Price Point)
 OTE for the people who actually do the work: $120K–$200K+ annually
 The top performers here aren't just closers. 
They're portfolio builders. 
Every month you close, you're stacking another stream of recurring income on top of what you closed last month. 
Twelve months in, you've got a book of business that pays you whether you take the call or not.
 Sound familiar?
 That's right. 
We pay you the same way we teach our clients to live. 
Passive income. Compounding. Freedom.
 If we wouldn't drink our own Kool-Aid with the people who sell our offer, we'd have no business selling it to anyone.
 What's In It For The Right Person. 
 Beyond the money?
 Mission that matters. You'll be the first conversation thousands of families ever have about real financial freedom. You'll be the one who makes them realize they've been lied to for thirty years, and you'll be the one who shows them the way out.
 Direct access to Russ Morgan and Joey Muré, two of the most generous, mission-driven, real-deal humans in this industry.
 Elite-level sales coaching from closers who've done eight figures in this exact niche.
 100% remote. From your kitchen. From Bali. From a coffee shop in Medellín. We don't care where the work happens. We care that the work happens.
 Pre-qualified, warm inbound leads — not cold lists, not scraped data, not random dials.
 A real product you can be proud of. No bait-and-switch. No fake scarcity. No "course that goes nowhere." A genuine pathway to freedom backed by a decade of results.

 6 Month Contract
